transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Marcus Nguyen (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dana Ruiz (Arbor Head of Security), Tom Becker (Platform Eng), Riley Chen (DevOps), Lina Ugor (Legal)

Summary:
High-level alignment on SSO provisioning (SAML + SCIM), least-privilege RBAC mapping, KMS/encryption requirements, and audit log retention/residency. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share certs and SCIM templates; Arbor to share RBAC matrix and schedule canary POC.

Topics:
- SAML IdP metadata exchange and assertion attributes
- SCIM user/group sync and mapping to roles
- RBAC role design: least-privilege vs admin bundles
- Audit logging, retention, and residency (EU vs US)
- Encryption at rest and KMS integration options
- Network constraints for private deployments / VPC peering

Transcript body:
[00:00] Marcus: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Marcus from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dana: Good, thanks. Busy week but we're ready to get through the SSO and RBAC stuff.
[00:12] Priya: Awesome, we'll try to keep this focused. Quick agenda: confirm SAML flows, SCIM mapping, RBAC role set, and then KMS / logging questions. Anything to add?
[00:22] Tom: Maybe a quick note on our timeline — we need a POC by end of May so timing is tight.
[00:27] Marcus: Got it, that frames the priorities.
[00:30] Riley: Quick note — our infra team uses Google Workspace for IdP, but we also have Azure AD for some partners, so we need Brownfield support for multiple IdPs.
[00:40] Priya: That's fine, Redwood supports multiple SAML IdPs per org and you can map them to SCIM groups. One detail: our SCIM connector expects group membership in the 'members' array, and we recommend syncing group->role bindings from your side for least privilege.
[00:52] Dana: When you say 'map to role bindings' — can you show an example? We're trying to avoid overprivileged roles.
[00:57] Priya: Sure, I'll share a simple mapping in the deck after the call, but quick example: SCIM group 'arbor-data-analysts' maps to Redwood role 'embedding-reader' which allows embeddings read and create but not model deployment or admin APIs.
[01:12] Tom: Are roles customizable? We want to restrict token creation to a small set of service accounts.
[01:17] Marcus: Yes, roles are pluggable. You can create custom roles and also disable token creation via RBAC policy. For tenants on Dedicated/Private we also recommend service-account-only tokens tied to KMS-wrapped keys.
[01:30] Riley: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys? Our security team insists on CMKs in Cloud KMS or on-prem HSM.
[01:36] Priya: We support KMS integrations for Private deployments; hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys or integrate with a BYOK flow — sorry, the exact acronym might be by O K — by that I mean bring-your-own-key. For Private we can do HSM-backed keys and enforce key policies.
[01:52] Dana: What about audit logs? We need immutable logs for at least 12 months and they must be stored in EU for our EU tenant.
[02:00] Marcus: We're able to route audit logs to your cloud storage via Kinesis/SQS or direct S3-compatible endpoints. We also support regionally resident logging for Private deployments; retention is configurable up to multiple years.
[02:14] Lina (Legal): Any issues with PII in logs? We need guidance on redaction and retention that meets GDPR.
[02:21] Priya: Good point. Our logs are configurable to redact request bodies by default; token-level tracing is available but can be disabled. We recommend sending application-level logs to your SIEM for long-term retention, and we can provide a hashed user identifier for correlation without raw PII.
[02:38] Dana: Walk me through the SAML attribute mapping — we need user email, role, and department, but our IdP uses 'eduPersonAffiliation' for some accounts and that trips mapping sometimes.
[02:48] Priya: We often see that. Our SCIM and SAML mappers are flexible; for SAML you can remap assertion attributes on the IdP side or use a Redwood mapping layer to canonicalize attributes. We'll send a sample mapping file.
[03:02] Tom: Do you support SCIM 2.0 PATCH and partial updates? We don't want full syncs for every change.
[03:09] Priya: Yes, SCIM 2.0 PATCH is supported. We also accept incremental events for group membership updates which reduces sync overhead.
[03:18] Riley: About RBAC — we want separation of duties: service accounts, data scientists, app ops, and platform admins. What granularity can Redwood handle?
[03:27] Marcus: Role granularity is pretty fine. You can carve permissions by API surface (generate, embeddings, model admin, billing views). You can also set resource-level ACLs to limit which models or routes a role can hit.
[03:40] Dana: If we have multiple teams in the EU and US, can we enforce residency rules per-team?
[03:46] Priya: With Dedicated or Private yes — you can pin models and storage to regions. Hosted can also route data to regional clusters, but Private gives you full control over residency and networking.
[03:58] Tom: Network — we need to ensure egress only to our VPC and have restricted IP ranges. Does Redwood support VPC peering or private endpoints?
[04:06] Marcus: Both. For Private we do VPC peering and private endpoint support; for Hosted we can provide private endpoints with IP allow lists and VPC egress configs in some cloud regions. We'll follow up with the networking checklist.
[04:20] Riley: Encryption at rest — how is the token database protected? If a token is created, can it be scoped to a specific model or route?
[04:30] Priya: Tokens are stored encrypted at rest; on Private you can wire your KMS. Tokens can be scoped with granular permissions and TTLs. Also for Dedicated we can do short-lived keys and rotate them.
[04:43] Dana: About SOC2 — do you have the Type II report readily shareable? We need it to progress procurement.
[04:49] Marcus: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 certs. I'll send redacted copies and the attestation letter. Expect in your inbox by 2026-05-18.
[04:58] Lina: Legal will also want the DPA; do you have a standard DPA or negotiable terms?
[05:03] Marcus: We have a standard DPA and can discuss narrow changes through legal. I'll include the DPA link with the security packet.
[05:11] Tom: One technical question: if we disable SCIM and do manual provisioning, can we still enforce SAML-only auth for interactive users?
[05:19] Priya: Yes. SCIM is optional. You can do SAML-only for interactive users and use service accounts or API keys provisioned via the console for automation.
[05:28] Riley: We'd prefer SCIM for automated deprovisioning to avoid orphaned accounts.
[05:31] Dana: Same — deprovisioning is a blocker for us.
[05:33] Priya: Agreed, that's best practice. We'll share the SCIM mapping and an example provisioning flow.
[05:40] Tom: For the RBAC matrix, do you have a recommended least-privilege starter kit?
[05:45] Marcus: We have a starter role set: admin, platform-ops, data-analyst, eng-service, read-only. We'll share the starter role definitions; customers often further split them.
[05:55] Dana: Any logs stored outside the tenant region for hosted mode? We worry about backups in US region if primary is EU.
[06:02] Priya: For Hosted we can configure backups and logs to stay in-region for EU tenants; we'll confirm specifics in the security packet. With Private it's fully under your control.
[06:12] Lina: Are there legal hold capabilities on logs if we have an investigation?
[06:16] Marcus: Yes, we can freeze retention policies on request for investigations — needs a support SLA and approvals. We'll outline the process.
[06:25] Riley: For the canary POC, what performance and telemetry will you expose? We need latency, token usage, and per-route error rates.
[06:33] Priya: Console exposes per-route latency, token breakdowns, tail latency percentiles, and error traces. For dedicated POCs we'll give a temporary dashboard with live tracing.
[06:43] Tom: Regarding the POC tenant, can we test model fallback policies — like if the p99 spikes, fallback to cheaper model?
[06:51] Priya: Yes, routing policies can be configured for fallback by latency or cost. We'll demo that in the POC.
[06:58] Dana: Any gotchas around SAML session length and SCIM sync frequency? Our sessions are 8 hours by policy.
[07:05] Priya: We support configurable session lengths; default is often 8 hours but you can adjust TTL. SCIM sync frequency can be near-real-time via event hooks or periodic cron syncs.
[07:15] Marcus: Okay, quick recap of agreed items and owners...
[07:20] Marcus: Action items: I'll send SOC2/ISO and DPA, Priya will send SCIM mapping and SAML metadata example, Tom will export RBAC matrix, Riley will confirm KMS choices, and we'll schedule the canary POC start date.
[07:36] Dana: Sounds good. A couple of quick questions from Legal — Lina: are there indemnities for data exfil in the standard contract?
[07:43] Lina: we just need to flag those now — not asking for negotiation in this meeting.
[07:47] Marcus: We'll include the contract summary; legal can follow up.
[07:51] Tom: Can you also share an architecture diagram of Private deployment network flow? That will help infra signoff.
[07:58] Priya: Yep, we'll attach the network diagram in the follow-up packet.
[08:02] Riley: One tiny thing — SCIM group name normalization. We use lowercase dashes; can Redwood handle that?
[08:08] Priya: Yes, we can canonicalize group names on ingest.
[08:12] Dana: If we need RBAC changes mid-POC, how fast can they be applied?
[08:16] Marcus: Role changes propagate in seconds for hosted; on Private they'll depend on your deployment but generally within a minute.
[08:24] Tom: For the canary, we'll lock down the service-account roles to avoid accidental deploys.
[08:29] Marcus: Good plan. Any final questions?
[08:32] Lina: One last legal note: please redact any customer data in the SOC2 docs prior to share.
[08:36] Marcus: Will do.
[08:37] Dana: Alright thanks everyone, looking forward to the materials.
[08:40] Marcus: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the packet and a calendar invite for the POC kickoff.
[08:45] Tom: Thanks.
[58:00] End of recording
